activities.title: Sketch how fatigue feels
activities.subtitle: Pick a colour that matches how your body feels. Fill the page slowly.

activities.title: Draw your safe place
activities.subtitle: Sketch a place where you feel completely safe.

activities.title: Doodle patterns to music
activities.subtitle: Soft playlist on. Let your hand move without a plan.

activities.title: Draw what hope looks like
activities.subtitle: Hope doesn't have to be pretty. Draw shapes that represent it.

activities.title: Sketch a window view
activities.subtitle: Draw what you wish you could see outside. Let it take you somewhere restorative.

activities.title: Draw flowers from memory
activities.subtitle: How many flowers can you draw from memory? Let it become a garden.

activities.title: Sketch your hands
activities.subtitle: Look at your hands and draw them as they are. They have carried you through so much.

activities.title: Draw emotions as weather
activities.subtitle: Is today a storm, a fog, a clearing sky? Draw the weather of your emotion.

activities.title: Blind contour drawing
activities.subtitle: Pick any object nearby. Draw it without looking at the paper.

activities.title: Draw the people who love you
activities.subtitle: Sketch the faces of people who have shown up for you. Simple shapes are perfect. Photograph your drawing when done — it's a keeper.

activities.title: Fill a page with circles
activities.subtitle: No corners, no edges. Just slow circles. Let your hand rest.

activities.title: Sketch your window view
activities.subtitle: Look outside and draw exactly what you see.

activities.title: Draw what 'rest' looks like
activities.subtitle: What does true rest look like to you? A hammock, still water? Draw it.

activities.title: Zentangle, repeating patterns
activities.subtitle: Draw a square and fill it with any repeating pattern.

activities.title: Draw your journey as a road
activities.subtitle: Where did it start? Where are you now? Draw it however it feels true.

activities.title: Sketch what made you smile
activities.subtitle: Even a cup of tea, a bird, a message from someone. Draw it from memory.

activities.title: Free doodle, no thinking
activities.subtitle: No goal, no subject. Just let the pen move wherever it wants for 5 minutes.

activities.title: Draw your favourite season
activities.subtitle: Leaves, snowflakes, sunshine, rain — the season that makes you feel most yourself.

activities.title: Draw a mandala
activities.subtitle: Draw a dot in the middle and add rings of shapes. Go as slowly as you need.

activities.title: Portrait of someone you love
activities.subtitle: Draw someone's face from memory. Imperfect is perfect. It's the love that counts.

activities.title: Paint mood in two colours
activities.subtitle: Pick two colours that reflect how you feel. Layer them and let them tell the story.

activities.title: Watercolour wash
activities.subtitle: Wet the paper and drop colour onto it. Watch it move and merge on its own.

activities.title: Paint a sunrise from memory
activities.subtitle: Layer orange, pink, purple, yellow. No photo needed — paint the sky from memory.

activities.title: Paint what music makes you feel
activities.subtitle: Put on a song and paint shapes and colours that match what you hear.

activities.title: Paint a tree in healing
activities.subtitle: Bare, budding, or in bloom? Paint the tree that represents where you are now. Photograph it when done and save it to your memories.

activities.title: Finger painting, no brushes
activities.subtitle: Use your fingers to spread paint. Direct contact is grounding.

activities.title: Paint the view from your bed
activities.subtitle: Whatever you see from where you rest most. Capture this ordinary, precious view.

activities.title: Gratitude painting
activities.subtitle: Paint whatever you're grateful for. Let the canvas become a visual thank-you.

activities.title: Paint the sea
activities.subtitle: Blue, grey, turquoise — paint a body of water that matches your mood.

activities.title: Paint your strength
activities.subtitle: What does your strength look like? Bold lines, a mountain, a flame? Paint it.

activities.title: Monochrome painting
activities.subtitle: Pick one colour and explore every shade — light to dark. Simple and satisfying.

activities.title: Paint a garden you love
activities.subtitle: Flowers, trees, a bench — paint the outdoor space that feels most peaceful.

activities.title: Splatter painting
activities.subtitle: Flick paint onto the page. Let it be messy and free. Sometimes you need that.

activities.title: Paint nature you're missing
activities.subtitle: A forest, a beach, a garden. Paint it and let yourself be there a moment.

activities.title: Paint tonight's sky
activities.subtitle: Deep blue, scattered stars, moonlight or overcast — paint the sky above you tonight.

activities.title: Paint your favourite food
activities.subtitle: Vivid colours, texture, warmth — paint a meal or food that brings you pure comfort.

activities.title: Abstract colour field
activities.subtitle: Divide the page into sections and fill each with a different colour.

activities.title: Paint a bird in flight
activities.subtitle: One bird, open sky. Freedom and movement painted gently.

activities.title: Paint your most peaceful place
activities.subtitle: Close your eyes, go there, then paint it from feeling rather than memory.

activities.title: Loose floral painting
activities.subtitle: Paint flowers loosely. Overlapping petals, imperfect shapes. Loose and alive.

activities.title: Body scan, no judgment
activities.subtitle: Lie still. Move attention slowly up your body, noticing sensation without judgment. Afterwards, jot one word about how you feel and photograph it as a small record of the moment.

activities.title: 5-4-3-2-1 grounding practice
activities.subtitle: 5 you see, 4 you touch, 3 you hear, 2 you smell, 1 you taste. Fully present.

activities.title: Loving-kindness for your body
activities.subtitle: Silently say: 'May my body be at ease. May it heal. May it feel safe.'

activities.title: Visualise healing light
activities.subtitle: Imagine warm light entering at your head and moving slowly through you. Afterwards, find one object nearby that matches the colour you visualised and photograph it.

activities.title: Counting breath, count to 10
activities.subtitle: Count each exhale from 1 to 10, then restart. When your mind wanders, gently return.

activities.title: Open awareness
activities.subtitle: Sit quietly. Watch thoughts pass like clouds. You don't need to hold any of them.

activities.title: Gratitude meditation
activities.subtitle: Recall three moments you're grateful for. Hold each one for a full breath. Then photograph one thing nearby that represents any of those three moments.

activities.title: RAIN meditation
activities.subtitle: Recognise what you feel. Allow it. Investigate with kindness. Nurture yourself.

activities.title: Candle gazing
activities.subtitle: Gently focus on a candle flame or any still object. Let your mind quiet around it.

activities.title: Progressive muscle relaxation
activities.subtitle: Tense each muscle group for 5 seconds, then release. Start from your feet.

activities.title: Loving-kindness for someone
activities.subtitle: Bring someone who helped you to mind. Silently wish them well. Notice how it feels.

activities.title: Sound meditation
activities.subtitle: Close your eyes. Listen to whatever sounds are here. Receive them as pure sensation.

activities.title: Visualise end of treatment
activities.subtitle: Close your eyes and picture the day treatment ends — who's there, what you do first.

activities.title: Acceptance, this is how it is
activities.subtitle: For each difficulty, breathe and say: this is how it is right now. Not forever.

activities.title: 3-minute sitting meditation
activities.subtitle: Set a 3-minute timer. Sit still and breathe. Nothing to do, nowhere to go.

activities.title: Walking meditation
activities.subtitle: Walk very slowly across the room. Feel each foot on the floor. Repeat.

activities.title: Breath awareness
activities.subtitle: No need to change your breath. Just observe it. Notice where you feel it most.

activities.title: Morning intention, one word
activities.subtitle: Sit for a moment. Choose one word to guide today — rest, courage, gentle.

activities.title: Self-compassion pause
activities.subtitle: Hand on heart. Say: 'This is hard. I am doing my best. I am not alone.'

activities.title: Evening wind-down
activities.subtitle: Lie down and notice each part of your body. Give each part permission to rest.

activities.title: 5-minute slow walk
activities.subtitle: Set a 5-minute timer and walk slowly. Count each step. No distance goal. Photograph one thing that catches your eye along the way.

activities.title: Walk to end of the street
activities.subtitle: One small loop. Notice three things you haven't looked at carefully before.

activities.title: Nature walk
activities.subtitle: Name every plant, bird, and insect you pass. Let nature pull you out of your head. Photograph the one thing that made you pause longest.

activities.title: Gratitude walk
activities.subtitle: One grateful thing per step. Small or large. Keep going until you run out of steps.

activities.title: Walk somewhere comforting
activities.subtitle: A park bench, a garden, a friend's house. Walk toward something that feels good. Take a photo when you arrive — this is a place worth remembering.

activities.title: Indoor corridor walk
activities.subtitle: Walk slowly between rooms. Even 10 minutes of gentle indoor movement counts.

activities.title: Walk after a meal
activities.subtitle: A 10-minute walk after eating helps digestion, energy, and mood. Let your body lead.

activities.title: Sensory walk, all five senses
activities.subtitle: Each minute, focus on one sense. Sight, then sound, touch, smell, taste. Rotate.

activities.title: Walk without a destination
activities.subtitle: No route planned. Turn wherever feels right. Reclaim aimless movement.

activities.title: Sunrise or sunset walk
activities.subtitle: Walk during the golden hour. Let the changing light be the point of the whole walk.

activities.title: Walk barefoot on grass
activities.subtitle: If you can, take your shoes off and feel the ground. Grounding is deeply calming.

activities.title: Walk with someone, no agenda
activities.subtitle: Ask someone to walk with you. No goal, no plan — just walk and talk.

activities.title: Photograph walk
activities.subtitle: Walk until you find one thing worth photographing. One image is the whole goal.

activities.title: Stretch walk
activities.subtitle: Walk 5 minutes, stop and stretch gently, then walk again. Movement and release.

activities.title: Celebratory walk
activities.subtitle: Walk as celebration. Every step is a small defiance of everything you've faced.

activities.title: Mindful walk
activities.subtitle: Walk at half your usual pace. Nowhere to be. Just be here, moving.

activities.title: Morning walk
activities.subtitle: Step outside before the day gets busy. Fresh air, quiet streets, soft light.

activities.title: Walk after hard news
activities.subtitle: When feelings are too big to sit with, walk them out. Let your legs carry it.

activities.title: Window-shopping walk
activities.subtitle: Walk past shops and storefronts. Enjoy what you see without pressure.

activities.title: Neighbourhood walk
activities.subtitle: Walk a street you don't usually take. Find something you've never noticed.

activities.title: Read one short poem, twice
activities.subtitle: Find a short poem. Read it once for words, once for feeling. Let it land.

activities.title: Read a light chapter
activities.subtitle: A novel, a memoir, a feel-good story — something that takes you somewhere else.

activities.title: Read one neglected page
activities.subtitle: Open a book you left half-read. Just one page. Reconnect with it.

activities.title: Read a survivor's story
activities.subtitle: A memoir, a blog, an interview. Let someone else's 'I made it' be something to hold.

activities.title: Read about a dream destination
activities.subtitle: Travel writing or a blog — let yourself dream about somewhere beautiful.

activities.title: Reread an old favourite
activities.subtitle: A childhood book, an old favourite. Let familiarity be comfort.

activities.title: Read one short story through
activities.subtitle: A complete short story — 15 to 30 minutes. Finishing something matters right now.

activities.title: Read letters to the ill
activities.subtitle: Letters written to patients, essays on healing. Others have walked this path.

activities.title: Read something funny
activities.subtitle: A comic strip, a funny essay, a humorous book. Laughter does something real.

activities.title: Read about healing
activities.subtitle: A book or article about how the body heals. Understanding can feel less frightening.

activities.title: Read a nature essay
activities.subtitle: Something about birds, forests, or oceans. Nature writing is calming and absorbing.

activities.title: Browse a cookbook
activities.subtitle: Flick through recipes, look at photos. The pleasure of food without any effort.

activities.title: Read quotes about courage
activities.subtitle: Find quotes that feel true to what you're going through. Write down the best one.

activities.title: Browse something purely visual
activities.subtitle: A photography magazine, a design blog, an art book. Low demand, high pleasure.

activities.title: Read your next chapter
activities.subtitle: Don't overthink it — just pick up your current book and read the next chapter.

activities.title: Browse something curious
activities.subtitle: Pick something you've always wanted to know more about. Spend 20 minutes reading.

activities.title: Read in bed
activities.subtitle: Get comfortable with your book. Let reading be the whole activity, not a prelude.

activities.title: Read a children's book
activities.subtitle: Simple language, beautiful images, gentle wisdom. No age requirement for comfort.

activities.title: Read an essay you love
activities.subtitle: A well-written piece on something that interests you. Give it your full attention.

activities.title: Read outside or near a window
activities.subtitle: Take your book somewhere with fresh air. Reading outdoors is restorative.

activities.title: Make a chemo comfort playlist
activities.subtitle: Build a playlist for treatment days. Songs that feel like a hand on your shoulder.

activities.title: Classical music, eyes closed
activities.subtitle: Choose a slow orchestral piece — Debussy, Satie, Bach. Let it be the only thing.

activities.title: Listen to nature sounds
activities.subtitle: Find a nature soundscape. Let the sound take you somewhere natural.

activities.title: An album from happier times
activities.subtitle: Pick an album from a time life felt good. Let the music return you to that self.

activities.title: Binaural or healing music
activities.subtitle: Search for 528Hz or theta wave music. Lie down and let the frequency work on you.

activities.title: Listen to childhood music
activities.subtitle: Songs from school, road trips, holidays. Let them reconnect you to who you were.

activities.title: Listen to a gentle film score
activities.subtitle: Film scores from Ghibli, Hans Zimmer, Morricone. Emotional, beautiful, no lyrics.

activities.title: Playlist for who you're becoming
activities.subtitle: Songs that represent where you want to be — recovered, fully yourself again.

activities.title: Music and a hand massage
activities.subtitle: Put on a soft playlist and slowly massage your hands and wrists.

activities.title: One song, three times through
activities.subtitle: Pick a song that matches your mood. Listen three times. Fully inhabit it.

activities.title: A music podcast you love
activities.subtitle: Not just music — a conversation about it. Something for gentle company.

activities.title: Listen to lo-fi while resting
activities.subtitle: Lo-fi, ambient, or soft electronic. No peaks, no lyrics. Just texture.

activities.title: Music from a meaningful place
activities.subtitle: Music rooted in a place connected to your history or family. Let it root you.

activities.title: Guided relaxation with music
activities.subtitle: Find a guided relaxation with background music. Let a voice and melody carry you.

activities.title: One song, what memory comes?
activities.subtitle: Let a song play and notice what it brings up. A person, a place, a feeling.

activities.title: Soft playlist, no screens
activities.subtitle: Music on, phone face down, eyes closed. Nothing else. Just you and the sound.

activities.title: Play your favourite song
activities.subtitle: The one song that always works. Play it. Let it do what it does.

activities.title: Morning music ritual
activities.subtitle: One calming song as your morning anchor. The same song each day builds ritual.

activities.title: Instrumental jazz
activities.subtitle: Soft jazz piano or trio. Warmth without demanding your attention.

activities.title: A playlist for someone you love
activities.subtitle: Curate a playlist as a gift. A quiet act of love that also nourishes you.

activities.title: Make ginger tea from scratch
activities.subtitle: Fresh ginger in hot water with honey and lemon. Drink slowly. It helps with nausea. Take a photo of your cup before you drink it.

activities.title: Cook a simple warming soup
activities.subtitle: Warm broth with soft vegetables. Easy on the stomach. Let the process be slow. Photograph your bowl before eating — nourishment worth remembering.

activities.title: Bake banana bread or muffins
activities.subtitle: The smell of baking, the result you can share. Low complexity, high reward.

activities.title: Blend a healing smoothie
activities.subtitle: Blend banana, ginger, turmeric, and coconut milk. Gentle on the stomach. Take a photo of it before your first sip — colour is part of the comfort.

activities.title: Cook your comfort food
activities.subtitle: The meal that means comfort. Make it exactly as you remember.

activities.title: Herbal tea, note each feeling
activities.subtitle: Chamomile, peppermint, rooibos. Brew each one and notice how it feels in your body.

activities.title: Cook a meal as a gift
activities.subtitle: Cook something and give it away. Feeding others fills you too.

activities.title: Try an anti-inflammatory recipe
activities.subtitle: Turmeric, greens, berries, olive oil. One simple recipe to support recovery.

activities.title: A recipe from someone dear
activities.subtitle: A grandmother's dish, a family recipe. Cook it as a way of being close to them.

activities.title: A nourishing breakfast
activities.subtitle: Warm oats, poached eggs, fresh fruit — whatever nourishes most. Eat without rushing.

activities.title: Soft-texture meal
activities.subtitle: Mashed, steamed, or blended. When nausea is present, soft food made with care helps.

activities.title: Make golden milk or chai
activities.subtitle: Turmeric milk, cinnamon chai, spiced cocoa. Warming, aromatic, deeply soothing.

activities.title: Cook something colourful
activities.subtitle: Roasted vegetables, a vivid bowl. When appetite is low, colour helps the first bite.

activities.title: Batch cook for rest days
activities.subtitle: Make a double portion and store the rest. Future you will be grateful.

activities.title: Fruit ice cubes for nausea
activities.subtitle: Freeze lemon, mint, or ginger into ice cubes. They help with nausea and dry mouth.

activities.title: Make your favourite drink
activities.subtitle: Make it the right way, cup it in your hands, and drink it slowly. Nothing else.

activities.title: One-pot meal, minimal effort
activities.subtitle: One pot, a few ingredients, 20 minutes. You deserve to eat well without the effort.

activities.title: Cook while listening
activities.subtitle: Two gentle activities at once. Cooking in the background, your mind entertained.

activities.title: Make a small sweet treat
activities.subtitle: A few cookies, a small cake, a pudding. You are allowed sweetness. Enjoy every bite.

activities.title: Follow a new recipe
activities.subtitle: Pick a recipe you've never made. Follow each step. Let the process absorb you.

activities.title: Call someone to just listen
activities.subtitle: Tell them first: I just need you to listen. Then say what's really on your mind.

activities.title: Tell someone what helped you
activities.subtitle: Not 'thanks for everything' — but 'when you did that, it helped in this way.'

activities.title: Video call someone you've missed
activities.subtitle: Isolation drifts into distance. Reach out to someone you miss — a face helps. Take a screenshot of the call or snap a photo of yourself after. You showed up.

activities.title: Ask someone for a happy memory
activities.subtitle: Call someone and ask: tell me a happy memory. Just listen. Let their past warm you.

activities.title: Tell your family what you need
activities.subtitle: Not 'I need support' — but 'I need dinner Thursday.' Specific asks are easier.

activities.title: Share how treatment is going
activities.subtitle: Tell someone the unfiltered truth. Not to protect them — let them hold it.

activities.title: Talk about life, not illness
activities.subtitle: Ask about their week, a show they're watching. Let it be a normal conversation.

activities.title: Voice note to someone you miss
activities.subtitle: If a call feels like too much right now, record a short voice message for someone you've been thinking of. Your voice reaching them is enough.

activities.title: Tell someone you love them
activities.subtitle: Text, call, or say it in person. Three words. Always worth saying now.

activities.title: Share a fear you've held alone
activities.subtitle: Choose one person who can hold it. Say: I've been afraid to tell you something.

activities.title: Ask someone to just be with you
activities.subtitle: Ask someone to come or stay on a call with no plan. Just presence. Silence counts.

activities.title: Call someone who knows hardship
activities.subtitle: Reach out to someone who knows hard times. Let them remind you they came through.

activities.title: Plan something to look forward to
activities.subtitle: Name a future moment — a meal, a trip. Having something ahead genuinely helps.

activities.title: Share a funny memory together
activities.subtitle: Ask: what's the funniest memory you have of us? Let laughter be the whole point.

activities.title: Ask someone to read to you
activities.subtitle: A chapter, a poem, an article. Ask them to read it while you close your eyes.

activities.title: Check in on someone today
activities.subtitle: Genuinely asking how someone else is can take you out of your own pain briefly.

activities.title: Share something you're proud of
activities.subtitle: Something you've done or endured. Say: I wanted to tell you I'm proud of myself.

activities.title: Send a voice message to someone
activities.subtitle: Pick someone specific — a parent, a friend, a sibling. Record what you want to say and send it. Your voice carries more warmth than any text. Snap a photo of the message sent as a small memory.

activities.title: Call, say you're thinking of them
activities.subtitle: No agenda. Just: I was thinking of you and wanted to hear your voice. That's it.

activities.title: Watch a show together remotely
activities.subtitle: Sync up on a show and watch together remotely. Shared experience without talking.

activities.title: Repot an overdue plant
activities.subtitle: A slow, grounding task. New soil, new space — tending growth when you need it.

activities.title: Plant seeds and watch them grow
activities.subtitle: Sow seeds — herbs, flowers, vegetables. Tend to something growing alongside you.

activities.title: Tend your houseplants
activities.subtitle: A quiet indoor ritual. Water what needs it. Wipe the dust from the leaves.

activities.title: Deadhead flowers for new growth
activities.subtitle: Remove spent flowers so the plant puts energy into new growth. A gentle metaphor.

activities.title: Grow herbs on your windowsill
activities.subtitle: A small pot on a sunny ledge. Watching something edible grow and later nourish you.

activities.title: Sit outside and just observe
activities.subtitle: No weeding, no planting — just sit outside. A bee, a bird, the wind in the leaves.

activities.title: Press flowers into a page
activities.subtitle: Collect a few flowers and press them between books. In a week, something beautiful.

activities.title: Make a small terrarium
activities.subtitle: Layer stones, soil, and moss in a jar. A tiny world to keep by your bedside.

activities.title: Visit a garden or flower market
activities.subtitle: Surround yourself with green things. Even an hour among plants and flowers restores.

activities.title: Buy yourself one flower
activities.subtitle: Buy one flower just for yourself. Put it where you'll see it. You're worth that.

activities.title: Learn about one plant you own
activities.subtitle: Look up the origin and meaning of one plant you own. Where does it come from?

activities.title: Tend your outdoor herb garden
activities.subtitle: Trim, water, harvest a few leaves. The smell of fresh herbs is grounding.

activities.title: Read flower meanings
activities.subtitle: Look up flower symbolism. If you could send someone a bouquet, what would it say?

activities.title: Propagate a plant
activities.subtitle: Snip a stem, place in water and wait. Watching roots appear is quietly miraculous.

activities.title: Write care notes for each plant
activities.subtitle: Note what each plant needs — light, water, temperature. A gentle act of attention.

activities.title: Water your plants, talk to them
activities.subtitle: It sounds strange, but it works. Talk to your plants as you water them.

activities.title: Give a plant some fresh air
activities.subtitle: Even houseplants benefit from outdoor air. Move one outside for a few hours.

activities.title: Arrange flowers in a vase
activities.subtitle: A loose, imperfect arrangement. Nothing formal. Just life and colour in the room.

activities.title: Clear a patch of weeds
activities.subtitle: Pick one manageable patch. Clear it. The result is immediate and satisfying.

activities.title: Photograph your plants
activities.subtitle: Photograph your plants and compare to older photos. Growth takes time to notice.

activities.title: Gratitude paper chain
activities.subtitle: Write one grateful thing per strip and link them into a chain. Hang it visibly. Photograph it when done — it's worth keeping.

activities.title: Make a vision board
activities.subtitle: Cut out words and images that represent what you want after treatment.

activities.title: Fold origami, crane or flower
activities.subtitle: Origami asks for focused hands and a quiet mind. Repetition is meditative.

activities.title: Make a friendship bracelet
activities.subtitle: Three threads, a simple knot pattern, 15 minutes. Make it for yourself.

activities.title: Photo collage of loved ones
activities.subtitle: Arrange photos of your favourite people. A reminder of what you're holding onto.

activities.title: Knit or crochet a small square
activities.subtitle: Cast on and knit one small square. The rhythm is one of the most calming motions.

activities.title: Make cards for those who helped
activities.subtitle: Folded paper, a message, a small drawing. Handmade says more than anything bought.

activities.title: Make a paper flower bouquet
activities.subtitle: Fold or cut paper into simple flowers in colours that lift your mood.

activities.title: Decorate a journaling notebook
activities.subtitle: Decorate the cover with stickers or drawings. Make it yours before writing.

activities.title: Make a worry jar
activities.subtitle: Write each worry, fold it, put it in a jar. Externalising worry reduces its power.

activities.title: Make a simple bookmark
activities.subtitle: Cut and decorate a strip of card. Something useful you made. Complete satisfaction.

activities.title: Embroider a simple pattern
activities.subtitle: A flower, a word, a simple shape. Needle and thread on fabric. Slow and meditative.

activities.title: A scrapbook page of a memory
activities.subtitle: One page. Photos, tickets, notes, drawings. A single memory preserved with care.

activities.title: Build something with clay
activities.subtitle: Knead, shape, sculpt. Working clay with your hands is deeply grounding.

activities.title: Nature craft
activities.subtitle: Collect leaves, pebbles, or twigs and make something simple. Bring the outside in.

activities.title: Washi tape decorating
activities.subtitle: Washi tape is forgiving. Decorate something small and make it feel new.

activities.title: Tear paper and make a collage
activities.subtitle: No scissors needed. Tear coloured paper into shapes and arrange them. Tearing helps.

activities.title: Create with only what you have
activities.subtitle: Rubber bands, string, cardboard. What can you make from only what's around you?

activities.title: String a beaded bracelet
activities.subtitle: Sorting beads is repetitive and calming. You end with something wearable.

activities.title: Make something and give it away
activities.subtitle: A card, a drawing, a bracelet — something simple, given away. It satisfies deeply.

activities.title: Watch a nature documentary
activities.subtitle: Planet Earth, Blue Planet. When your world feels small, let the screen fill it.

activities.title: Rewatch a childhood favourite
activities.subtitle: A film you loved when young. Comfort, nostalgia, a reminder of who you were.

activities.title: Watch a film in a dream location
activities.subtitle: Italy, Japan, New Zealand — let the landscape take you somewhere gorgeous.

activities.title: Rewatch a comedy
activities.subtitle: A film you know is funny. No surprises — just laughter you know is coming.

activities.title: A film about beating the odds
activities.subtitle: A true story of survival or triumph. Let it remind you what human beings can do.

activities.title: Watch a short film
activities.subtitle: Find a short film. Something complete in 20 minutes. The satisfaction of finishing.

activities.title: Watch a cooking or baking show
activities.subtitle: The Great British Bake Off, Chef's Table. Food, warmth, and gentle competition.

activities.title: Watch a travel documentary
activities.subtitle: Let yourself travel without leaving your bed. New landscapes, new cultures.

activities.title: Watch a film you've postponed
activities.subtitle: The one you keep postponing. Today is the day. A film that has been waiting for you.

activities.title: Watch a musical
activities.subtitle: Hamilton, Mamma Mia, La La Land. Music, colour, and story combined.

activities.title: Watch a creativity documentary
activities.subtitle: A film about an artist, a band, or a photographer. Creative lives are absorbing.

activities.title: Watch a gentle romance
activities.subtitle: A love story with warmth and hope. Let the feeling exist alongside everything else.

activities.title: A film in another language
activities.subtitle: A French film, a Korean drama, an Italian classic. Let another culture's story in.

activities.title: Rewatch something for someone
activities.subtitle: A film tied to a memory with someone. Let yourself feel that connection again.

activities.title: Watch a wildlife documentary
activities.subtitle: Dogs, octopuses, lions. Animals doing extraordinary things. Uncomplicated enjoyment.

activities.title: Continue your current series
activities.subtitle: Pick up where you left off. Continuing characters you already know is comforting.

activities.title: Watch something funny tonight
activities.subtitle: A stand-up special, a sitcom, a comedy film. Laughter is medicine. Full permission.

activities.title: Start a recommended series
activities.subtitle: Text them: I'm watching it tonight. Watch episode one and message your thoughts.

activities.title: Watch with snacks
activities.subtitle: Make a plate of something good. Set up properly. Make the watching intentional.

activities.title: Watch a classic you've put off
activities.subtitle: A masterpiece you've never seen. Tonight is the night. Something waiting for you.

activities.title: Play a song from your childhood
activities.subtitle: A childhood song, played or sung. Comfort that bypasses the thinking mind.

activities.title: Improvise freely
activities.subtitle: Play whatever comes. No scales, no songs. Let the instrument voice what you feel.

activities.title: Learn one new chord or note
activities.subtitle: Learn just one new thing — one chord, one melody line. A tiny step forward.

activities.title: Sing a song you love, loudly
activities.subtitle: Sing as loudly as you want. Singing releases tension as much as crying does.

activities.title: Play a piece you know, slowly
activities.subtitle: Not to perform — to inhabit. Play something familiar much more slowly.

activities.title: Drum on a table or surface
activities.subtitle: Tap a rhythm on your table or legs. Rhythm is grounding. No instrument needed.

activities.title: Record yourself playing
activities.subtitle: Record a short clip on your phone. Not to share — just to hear yourself.

activities.title: Hum or whistle gently
activities.subtitle: Hum while you make tea or settle in. Continuous humming calms the nervous system.

activities.title: Play your very first song
activities.subtitle: Whatever your first song was. Return to the beginning. There is comfort there.

activities.title: Try a virtual keyboard app
activities.subtitle: GarageBand, a piano app, a virtual drum kit. Music needs no real instrument.

activities.title: Play a lullaby very softly
activities.subtitle: Something slow and tender. Play it the way you'd play for someone who needs comfort.

activities.title: Write one line of a song
activities.subtitle: Not a whole song — just one honest line. What would your first line be today?

activities.title: Play along to a song you love
activities.subtitle: Play alongside a recording. Even imperfect harmony with music you love is joyful.

activities.title: Clap and tap a rhythm
activities.subtitle: Tap your knees, clap softly, feel rhythm move through you. Minimal effort.

activities.title: Look up tabs for a loved song
activities.subtitle: Find the chords for one song. Learn just the first four bars. Start something.

activities.title: Play freely for 10 minutes
activities.subtitle: No structure, no goal. Play for 10 minutes. Let whatever is inside find its way out.

activities.title: Hum while breathing deeply
activities.subtitle: Breathe in, hum on the exhale. The vibration in your chest is calming and soothing.

activities.title: Sing in the shower
activities.subtitle: The acoustics are perfect. No audience. Sing whatever you want, as long as you like.

activities.title: Figure out chords by ear
activities.subtitle: Put on a song and try to work out the chords by ear. Engaging and satisfying.

activities.title: Sing or play for someone
activities.subtitle: Call someone and play or sing them something. The most personal gift you can give.

activities.title: Write a letter to your body
activities.subtitle: Address your body directly. Tell it how you feel. Say what you haven't been able to.

activities.title: Write a letter to your cancer
activities.subtitle: Anger, grief, defiance, exhaustion — write the letter you can't send. Say it all.

activities.title: Write about who you're becoming
activities.subtitle: Not who you were, not who you'll be — but who you are in the process of becoming.

activities.title: Record three things from today
activities.subtitle: Not feelings, not analysis — three things that happened. Ground yourself in the day.

activities.title: List 10 things you still want
activities.subtitle: Big or small, near or far. Things beyond treatment. Let yourself want things again.

activities.title: Write freely for 5 minutes
activities.subtitle: Set a timer and write without stopping or re-reading. Let the subconscious speak.

activities.title: A day before all this
activities.subtitle: Choose an ordinary day that feels precious in retrospect. Describe it fully.

activities.title: Write a gratitude list
activities.subtitle: Push past the obvious. Fresh water, a soft pillow, a friend who texted. Keep going.

activities.title: Write about your best day
activities.subtitle: Not an important day — the best day. What made it best? Who was there?

activities.title: Write to your future self
activities.subtitle: What do you hope they're doing? What do you want them to remember?

activities.title: Strength: then vs now
activities.subtitle: Has your definition of strength changed? What looks strong now that didn't before?

activities.title: List people who showed up
activities.subtitle: Name each person and what they did. Recording generosity is powerful.

activities.title: Your ideal recovery day
activities.subtitle: Paint it fully — where you are, who's there, how your body feels. Make it vivid.

activities.title: What the hardest moment taught
activities.subtitle: Not to silver-line it — but to look at what the hardest thing has given you.

activities.title: Write one true sentence
activities.subtitle: One sentence. It can be tiny or enormous. Just: one true thing about today.

activities.title: The story of your diagnosis
activities.subtitle: Describe that day from a slight distance. What happened? Who called? Where were you?

activities.title: List all you want to thank
activities.subtitle: To people, to experiences, to your own body. Thank-yous you don't need to send.

activities.title: A relationship that has changed
activities.subtitle: Better, harder, different, absent. How has one relationship shifted since diagnosis?

activities.title: What do people need to know?
activities.subtitle: Not what you say when asked. What you actually want them to know. Write it.

activities.title: Write about a moment of beauty
activities.subtitle: Light through a window, a kind gesture, a flower. Beauty alongside the hard.
